title: A store that survives Buen Fin
summary: An artisan cooperative from Tlaquepaque gets ten times its usual traffic during Buen Fin. The store must grow on its own and keep selling if a zone fails.

requirements.1: {{s1}} is each individual server: it has its own operating system the team patches, its inventory agent installed, and runs all day.
requirements.2: {{s2}} keeps 2 to 20 copies across both zones, adds or removes them with the load and replaces the ones that fail.
requirements.3: {{s3}} receives and decrypts HTTPS, sends /api to one group and /tienda to another, and only forwards to healthy servers.
requirements.4: {{s4}} obtains from a partner issuing authority, and automatically renews, what slot 3 presents to the browser to prove it is tienda.mx.
requirements.5: {{s5}} records CPU every minute and alerts the on-call team if it stays above 80 % for 5 minutes.
requirements.6: The managed database stores orders and inventory, and only the slot 1 servers query it.

s1.explanation: Each Azure Virtual Machines VM is one server that the team configures, patches and installs software on; the slot 2 scale set is the group that creates and manages those VMs.

s2.explanation: Virtual Machine Scale Sets creates identical VMs spread across zones, autoscale sets their number between a minimum and a maximum with the load, and failed VMs are replaced. An availability set only spreads VMs and does not scale.

s3.explanation: Application Gateway v2 terminates TLS, sends /api and /tienda to different backend pools with path rules and stops sending to backends that fail their health probe. Azure Load Balancer works at layer 4 and does not read the URL.
s3.hint_cue: sends /api to one group and /tienda to another

s4.explanation: Key Vault stores the tienda.mx certificate, requests it from a partner CA (DigiCert or GlobalSign) and renews it automatically; Application Gateway v2 checks for a new version every four hours. Managed HSM does not support certificates.
s4.hint_cue: presents to the browser to prove it is tienda.mx

s5.explanation: An Azure Monitor metric alert checks CPU every minute and fires its action group when the average stays above 80 % for 5 minutes. Azure Advisor only gives periodic recommendations.

azure-functions.s1: Azure Functions is a serverless solution that runs code from event-driven triggers: instead of deploying and maintaining servers, the team writes only the code and Azure handles the rest.

azure-availability-set.s2: An availability set spreads VMs across fault and update domains, but it does not add or remove VMs with the load.

azure-load-balancer.s3: Azure Load Balancer works at layer 4: it spreads TCP and UDP flows but does not decrypt HTTPS or read the URL.

azure-managed-hsm.s4: Managed HSM stores keys in a dedicated HSM, but it does not support certificates, which is what Application Gateway presents over HTTPS.

azure-advisor.s5: Azure Advisor analyzes the configuration and gives periodic recommendations; it does not watch CPU minute by minute or alert the on-call team.
